429	    /// undo step, and it routes through the binding like everything else, so
430	    /// applying one inside an action sets that action's end state.
431	    func presetSection() -> InspectorSection {
432	        var buttons: [NSView] = []
433	        for preset in TextPreset.all {
434	            buttons.append(
435	                OptionButtonControl(
436	                    title: preset.name,
437	                    action: { [weak self] in self?.apply(preset) },
438	                    enabled: { true }, onEdit: {}))
439	        }
440	        return InspectorSection(
441	            id: "text.presets", title: "Presets",
442	            defaultExpanded: false,
443	            rows: [
444	                inspectorButtonRow(Array(buttons.prefix(2))),
445	                inspectorButtonRow(Array(buttons.dropFirst(2))),
446	            ])
447	    }
448	
449	    private func apply(_ preset: TextPreset) {
450	        let canvas = binding.canvas
451	        let patches = preset.patches(on: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))
452	        binding.apply(
453	            preset.name, binding.ops(text: patches.text) + binding.ops(video: patches.video))
454	    }
455	}
456	
457	// MARK: - Presets
458	
459	/// One text preset (§4.3). Sizes and positions are FRACTIONS of the canvas so
460	/// a preset means the same thing on a 4K canvas as on a vertical one: a size
461	/// of the canvas's SHORT side, a position of its width and height (spec §11
462	/// VR-41), so a tall canvas gets the line height a wide one has.
463	struct TextPreset {
464	    let name: String
465	    let font: String
466	    let sizeFraction: Double
467	    let xFraction: Double
468	    let yFraction: Double
469	    let align: String
470	    let backdrop: BackdropProps?
471	    /// Of H, on a canvas taller than wide, in place of `yFraction` (the Caption
472	    /// row's 0.25, VR-41); nil keeps `yFraction` on every canvas.
473	    var tallYFraction: Double? = nil
474	
475	    /// The font size on `canvas`: `sizeFraction` of `min(W, H)`. On a canvas at
476	    /// least as wide as tall that is H, so the old `H × sizeFraction` is kept to the bit.
477	    func size(on canvas: CGSize) -> Double {
478	        (sizeFraction * Double(min(canvas.width, canvas.height))).rounded()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Where the box's centre sits on `canvas`.
482	    func position(on canvas: CGSize) -> (x: Double, y: Double) {
483	        let y = canvas.height > canvas.width ? tallYFraction ?? yFraction : yFraction
484	        return (xFraction * Double(canvas.width), y * Double(canvas.height))
485	    }
486	
487	    /// Text ▸ Presets' two patches: the face, size, alignment and backdrop, and where the
488	    /// box sits at full opacity.
489	    func patches(on canvas: CGSize) -> (text: TextPatch, video: VideoPatch) {
490	        let at = position(on: canvas)
491	        return (
492	            TextPatch(
493	                font: font, size: size(on: canvas), align: align, valign: "middle",
494	                backdrop: .some(backdrop)),
495	            VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)
496	        )
497	    }
498	
499	    static let all: [TextPreset] = [
500	        TextPreset(
501	            name: "Title", font: "SourceSans3-Bold", sizeFraction: 0.09, xFraction: 0,
502	            yFraction: 0, align: "center", backdrop: nil),
503	        TextPreset(
504	            name: "Subtitle", font: "SourceSans3-SemiBold", sizeFraction: 0.05, xFraction: 0,
505	            yFraction: 0.18, align: "center", backdrop: nil),
506	        TextPreset(
507	            name: "Lower Third", font: "SourceSans3-SemiBold", sizeFraction: 0.045,
508	            xFraction: -0.2, yFraction: 0.28, align: "left",
509	            backdrop: BackdropProps(color: [0, 0, 0, 0.55], padding: 18, radius: 6)),
510	        TextPreset(
511	            name: "Caption", font: "SourceSans3-Regular", sizeFraction: 0.035, xFraction: 0,
512	            yFraction: 0.38, align: "center",
513	            backdrop: BackdropProps(color: [0, 0, 0, 0.6], padding: 12, radius: 8),
514	            tallYFraction: 0.25),
515	    ]
516	}
517	
518	// MARK: - Faces
519	
520	/// The model's one font string ↔ the panel's family + style pair.
521	///
522	/// Everything here tolerates a name this machine has no font for: a project
523	/// carries PostScript names, and the Text tab still has to open (and still has
524	/// to be able to change the face) on a machine missing that family.
525	enum TextFace {
526	    /// Installed families, sorted. Read once — `availableFontFamilies` walks
527	    /// the font registry, and this popup is rebuilt on every selection change.
528	    static let families: [String] = NSFontManager.shared.availableFontFamilies.sorted()
529	
530	    /// One member of a family: its PostScript name and the style label.
531	    struct Member {
532	        let name: String
533	        let style: String
534	    }
535	
536	    static func members(of family: String) -> [Member] {
537	        let raw = NSFontManager.shared.availableMembers(ofFontFamily: family) ?? []
538	        return raw.compactMap { entry in
539	            guard entry.count >= 2, let name = entry[0] as? String,
540	                  let style = entry[1] as? String
541	            else { return nil }
542	            return Member(name: name, style: style)
543	        }
544	    }
545	
546	    /// The family a stored PostScript name belongs to; the first installed
547	    /// family when the font is missing, so the popup always has a row.
548	    static func family(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
549	        if let font = NSFont(name: postScriptName, size: 12), let family = font.familyName {
550	            return family
551	        }
552	        return families.first ?? "Helvetica"
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The style label of a stored name ("SemiBold"), or "Regular".
556	    static func style(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
557	        let family = family(of: postScriptName)
558	        return members(of: family).first { $0.name == postScriptName }?.style ?? "Regular"
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The PostScript name for a family plus a style label, keeping the style
562	    /// across a family change when the new family has one by that name.
563	    static func postScriptName(family: String, style: String) -> String {
564	        let list = members(of: family)
565	        if let match = list.first(where: { $0.style == style }) { return match.name }
566	        if let regular = list.first(where: { $0.style == "Regular" }) { return regular.name }
567	        return list.first?.name ?? family
568	    }
569	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of

  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);

  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map

  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),

  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

3	/// What a key does in the in-canvas text editor (spec §11 K-2,
4	/// kpgalligan/framejob#37): a bare Return applies, a modified Return is a new
5	/// line, Esc leaves or asks.
6	enum TextEditKeyRoute: Equatable {
7	    case apply, newline, escape
8	}
9	
10	enum TextEditKey {
11	    /// nil unless `event` is a key-down of Return (36), keypad Enter (76) or
12	    /// Esc (53) with no marked text — an input method owns all three while it
13	    /// composes. Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ is a new line, one rule for all
14	    /// four; ⇪, fn and the keypad flag are not modifiers here. Pure.
15	    static func route(_ event: NSEvent, hasMarkedText: Bool) -> TextEditKeyRoute? {
16	        guard event.type == .keyDown, !hasMarkedText else { return nil }
17	        switch event.keyCode {
18	        case 36, 76:
19	            let flags = event.modifierFlags.intersection(.deviceIndependentFlagsMask)
20	            let modifiers: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = [.shift, .command, .option, .control]
21	            return flags.intersection(modifiers).isEmpty ? .apply : .newline
22	        case 53:
23	            return .escape
24	        default:
25	            return nil
26	        }
27	    }
28	}

30	extension PreviewCanvasView {
31	    /// Esc in the editor. An unchanged string leaves at once; a changed one
32	    /// asks Cancel / Revert / Apply in a sheet, Apply the default (Return).
33	    ///
34	    /// The editor's blur-commit is suspended while the sheet is up — a blur
35	    /// that commits behind the question is the bug the sheet exists to
36	    /// prevent — and restored on Cancel. The completion is not an AppKit
37	    /// event, so Apply sends through `onGroupedEdit` (app/CLAUDE.md's undo
38	    /// pitfall); an editor torn down under the sheet (the clip removed by an
39	    /// agent) makes the answer a no-op.
40	    func escapeTextEditing() {
41	        guard let editor = textEditor, let id = editingClip, let window = window,
42	              snapshot.clip(id)?.text?.content != editor.string
43	        else {
44	            cancelTextEditing()
45	            return
46	        }
47	        let blur = editor.onBlur
48	        editor.onBlur = nil
49	        let alert = NSAlert()
50	        alert.messageText = "Apply your changes to this text?"
51	        alert.informativeText = "Return applies while you type; ⇧Return starts a new line."
52	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Apply")
53	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Revert")
54	        let cancel = alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
55	        cancel.keyEquivalent = "\u{1b}"
56	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self, weak editor] response in
57	            guard let self = self, let editor = editor, self.textEditor === editor else { return }
58	            switch response {
59	            case .alertFirstButtonReturn:
60	                let value = editor.string
61	                self.cancelTextEditing()
62	                guard let op = Self.textCommitOp(clip: id, value: value, in: self.snapshot)
63	                else { return }
64	                self.onGroupedEdit?("Edit Text", [op])
65	            case .alertSecondButtonReturn:
66	                self.cancelTextEditing()
67	            default:
68	                editor.onBlur = blur
69	                self.window?.makeFirstResponder(editor)
70	            }
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// The one op an in-canvas text commit sends — `finishTextEditing`'s
75	    /// Return or blur and the Esc sheet's Apply both build it here: nil when
76	    /// `id` is not in `snapshot`, has no text, or its base content already
77	    /// equals `value`; else one base `set_text` through
78	    /// `TextPatch.contentEdit`, so a timed page whose word count changes
79	    /// carries `words: []` beside the content and lands untimed instead of
80	    /// erroring (W-2). Pure, so a probe can call it.
81	    static func textCommitOp(clip id: UInt32, value: String,
82	                             in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> ReelOp? {
83	        guard let props = snapshot.clip(id)?.text, props.content != value else { return nil }
84	        return .setText(clips: [id], patch: TextPatch.contentEdit(value, over: props))
85	    }
86	}

4	/// The commands that put a clip on the timeline out of nothing rather than
5	/// out of a file already in the Media tab: Add Text (T), the Add Shape menu,
6	/// and — since road map 2's phase 6c — the two BACKGROUND commands.
7	///
8	/// Placement follows the spec §4.1 wording, "at the playhead": the clip goes on
9	/// the FRONT-MOST track if it fits there, and onto a new track above everything
10	/// if it does not. Trying the front track first is what keeps a title sequence
11	/// from growing a track per title; falling back to a new one is what keeps the
12	/// button from ever beeping at a playhead that happens to sit over a clip.
13	/// Both are one undo step either way, because `applyEdit` takes the whole op
14	/// list (`ProjectDocument`).
15	///
16	/// **The two background commands place nothing themselves.** A backdrop goes
17	/// on a NEW back-most track, which is a decision with a source window, a fill
18	/// scale and a `SCALE_MAX` clamp behind it, so the whole of it is one core op
19	/// — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`, argued at length in
20	/// `core/src/edit_background.rs`'s module doc. What is left here is the menu,
21	/// the open panel, and the one thing the core cannot answer: what should be
22	/// SELECTED afterwards.
23	extension EditorViewController {
24	
25	    /// T, the toolbar's Add Text button, and Clip > Add Text.
26	    @objc func addTextClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
27	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add Text") { track, at in
28	            .addTextClip(track: track, at: at)
29	        }
30	    }
31	
32	    /// One item of the Add Shape menu. The sender's tag indexes
33	    /// `ShapeKind.allCases` — the same tagging `showAddShapeMenu` writes, so
34	    /// the menu and the enum cannot drift.
35	    @objc func addShapeClipAtPlayhead(_ sender: Any?) {
36	        let kinds = ShapeKind.allCases
37	        let tag = (sender as? NSMenuItem)?.tag ?? 0
38	        let kind = tag >= 0 && tag < kinds.count ? kinds[tag] : .rectangle
39	        addGeneratedClip(named: "Add \(kind.displayName)") { track, at in
40	            .addShapeClip(track: track, at: at, shape: kind)
41	        }
42	    }
43	
44	    /// The shared body: place `make` on the front track, and if the core
45	    /// refuses it there — the overlap rule (§6) is the only reason it can —
46	    /// insert a track above everything and place it there instead.
47	    ///
48	    /// The refusal is detected by applying the op PURELY first, against the
49	    /// document's own handle. That costs one throwaway project value and keeps
50	    /// the fallback out of the undo stack: nothing is registered until the
51	    /// version that works is the one applied.
52	    ///
53	    /// `grouped` is for a caller running OFF-EVENT (a panel's completion):
54	    /// the edit goes through `performGroupedEdit`, else `applyEdit`.
55	    func addGeneratedClip(
56	        named name: String, grouped: Bool = false, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
57	    ) {
58	        guard let document = document else { return }
59	        // The EDITED project throughout, here and in every other command in
60	        // this file that places a clip: with a nest open the front track is
61	        // the NEST's front track, the overlap probe has to be run against the
62	        // nest, and the id set the selection is read back out of is the
63	        // nest's (road map 2's phase 9). `add_media` is the one exception and
64	        // is called out where it happens.
65	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
66	        let ops = Self.generatedClipOps(in: document, make)
67	        if grouped {
68	            document.performGroupedEdit(name, ops)
69	        } else {
70	            document.applyEdit(name, ops)
71	        }
72	        selectClips(addedSince: before, in: document)
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The track choice alone, no edit: `make` at the playhead on the
76	    /// edited project's front track when it fits there, else a new track
77	    /// above everything and `make` on it. `insert_graphic` places its clip
78	    /// by it too (spec §11 G-16 (a), G-45 (f)).
79	    static func generatedClipOps(
80	        in document: ProjectDocument, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp
81	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
82	        let before = document.editedProject.snapshot
83	        let at = document.playhead
84	        // `.project` on a `try?` collapses three answers into one nil: a
85	        // throw, an identity and a rule's refusal. Either way the front track
86	        // will not take this clip, so all of them take the new-track path.
87	        if let front = before.tracks.last?.id,
88	            (try? document.editedProject.applying(make(front, at))).project != nil
89	        {
90	            return [make(front, at)]
91	        }
92	        // The id of a newly added track is `next_id` from BEFORE the op —
93	        // the documented contract of the one JSON op entry point, since
94	        // `rc_project_apply` returns a project rather than an id.
95	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
96	        return [.addTrack(index: before.tracks.count), make(before.nextId, at)]
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Select whatever appeared, so the inspector opens on the new clip's own
100	    /// sections and the canvas draws its handles. Comparing id sets rather
101	    /// than trusting an id we predicted keeps this correct even if the core
102	    /// ever allocates differently — and it is why every command in this file
103	    /// reads the snapshot BEFORE it edits.
104	    ///
105	    /// Nothing added means the core refused or answered an identity —
106	    /// `applyEdit` has already beeped — so the selection stays as
107	    /// `ProjectDocument.clampViewState` left it.
108	    func selectClips(addedSince before: ProjectSnapshot, in document: ProjectDocument) {
109	        let existing = Set(before.clips.map { $0.id })
110	        let added = document.editedProject.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }
111	            .filter { !existing.contains($0) }
112	        guard !added.isEmpty else { return }
113	        document.selection = Set(added)
114	        viewStateDidChange()
115	    }

373	            id: "text.animation", title: "Reveal",

377	                    + String(format: " · %.2f s", ReelTime.seconds(animation.inDuration))

383	                inspectorPopupRow(
384	                    "Reveal", binding, name: "Text Animation", items: items,

388	                    },

390	                        guard index > 0, kinds.indices.contains(index - 1) else {

393	                        // The durations as they stand: switching the reveal
394	                        // must not reset the timing the user chose for it.
395	                        var a = current()
396	                        a.kind = kinds[index - 1]

402	                    quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],
403	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(current().inDuration) },
404	                    ops: { value in
405	                        var a = current()
406	                        a.inDuration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
407	                        return ops(a)

409	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.inDuration } },

413	                    max: 10, quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],

428	    /// and backdrop (text) plus where the box sits (video) — committed as ONE
429	    /// undo step, and it routes through the binding like everything else, so

432	        var buttons: [NSView] = []

450	        let canvas = binding.canvas
451	        let patches = preset.patches(on: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))

458	
459	/// One text preset (§4.3). Sizes and positions are FRACTIONS of the canvas so
460	/// a preset means the same thing on a 4K canvas as on a vertical one: a size
461	/// of the canvas's SHORT side, a position of its width and height (spec §11
462	/// VR-41), so a tall canvas gets the line height a wide one has.
463	struct TextPreset {
464	    let name: String
465	    let font: String
466	    let sizeFraction: Double
467	    let xFraction: Double
468	    let yFraction: Double
469	    let align: String
470	    let backdrop: BackdropProps?
471	    /// Of H, on a canvas taller than wide, in place of `yFraction` (the Caption
472	    /// row's 0.25, VR-41); nil keeps `yFraction` on every canvas.
473	    var tallYFraction: Double? = nil
474	
475	    /// The font size on `canvas`: `sizeFraction` of `min(W, H)`. On a canvas at
476	    /// least as wide as tall that is H, so the old `H × sizeFraction` is kept to the bit.
477	    func size(on canvas: CGSize) -> Double {
478	        (sizeFraction * Double(min(canvas.width, canvas.height))).rounded()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Where the box's centre sits on `canvas`.
482	    func position(on canvas: CGSize) -> (x: Double, y: Double) {
483	        let y = canvas.height > canvas.width ? tallYFraction ?? yFraction : yFraction
484	        return (xFraction * Double(canvas.width), y * Double(canvas.height))
485	    }
486	
487	    /// Text ▸ Presets' two patches: the face, size, alignment and backdrop, and where the
488	    /// box sits at full opacity.
489	    func patches(on canvas: CGSize) -> (text: TextPatch, video: VideoPatch) {
490	        let at = position(on: canvas)
491	        return (
492	            TextPatch(
493	                font: font, size: size(on: canvas), align: align, valign: "middle",
494	                backdrop: .some(backdrop)),
495	            VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)
496	        )
497	    }
498	
499	    static let all: [TextPreset] = [
500	        TextPreset(
501	            name: "Title", font: "SourceSans3-Bold", sizeFraction: 0.09, xFraction: 0,
502	            yFraction: 0, align: "center", backdrop: nil),
503	        TextPreset(
504	            name: "Subtitle", font: "SourceSans3-SemiBold", sizeFraction: 0.05, xFraction: 0,
505	            yFraction: 0.18, align: "center", backdrop: nil),
506	        TextPreset(
507	            name: "Lower Third", font: "SourceSans3-SemiBold", sizeFraction: 0.045,
508	            xFraction: -0.2, yFraction: 0.28, align: "left",
509	            backdrop: BackdropProps(color: [0, 0, 0, 0.55], padding: 18, radius: 6)),
510	        TextPreset(
511	            name: "Caption", font: "SourceSans3-Regular", sizeFraction: 0.035, xFraction: 0,
512	            yFraction: 0.38, align: "center",
513	            backdrop: BackdropProps(color: [0, 0, 0, 0.6], padding: 12, radius: 8),
514	            tallYFraction: 0.25),
515	    ]
516	}
517	
518	// MARK: - Faces
519	
520	/// The model's one font string ↔ the panel's family + style pair.
521	///
522	/// Everything here tolerates a name this machine has no font for: a project
523	/// carries PostScript names, and the Text tab still has to open (and still has
524	/// to be able to change the face) on a machine missing that family.
525	enum TextFace {
526	    /// Installed families, sorted. Read once — `availableFontFamilies` walks
527	    /// the font registry, and this popup is rebuilt on every selection change.
528	    static let families: [String] = NSFontManager.shared.availableFontFamilies.sorted()
529	
530	    /// One member of a family: its PostScript name and the style label.
531	    struct Member {
532	        let name: String
533	        let style: String
534	    }
535	
536	    static func members(of family: String) -> [Member] {
537	        let raw = NSFontManager.shared.availableMembers(ofFontFamily: family) ?? []
538	        return raw.compactMap { entry in
539	            guard entry.count >= 2, let name = entry[0] as? String,
540	                  let style = entry[1] as? String
541	            else { return nil }
542	            return Member(name: name, style: style)
543	        }
544	    }
545	
546	    /// The family a stored PostScript name belongs to; the first installed
547	    /// family when the font is missing, so the popup always has a row.
548	    static func family(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
549	        if let font = NSFont(name: postScriptName, size: 12), let family = font.familyName {
550	            return family
551	        }
552	        return families.first ?? "Helvetica"
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The style label of a stored name ("SemiBold"), or "Regular".
556	    static func style(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
557	        let family = family(of: postScriptName)
558	        return members(of: family).first { $0.name == postScriptName }?.style ?? "Regular"
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The PostScript name for a family plus a style label, keeping the style
562	    /// across a family change when the new family has one by that name.
563	    static func postScriptName(family: String, style: String) -> String {
564	        let list = members(of: family)
565	        if let match = list.first(where: { $0.style == style }) { return match.name }
566	        if let regular = list.first(where: { $0.style == "Regular" }) { return regular.name }
567	        return list.first?.name ?? family
568	    }
569	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

// ---- the burn-in timecode layer -----------------------------------------

/// The face a timecode burn-in is drawn in. A concrete face, not a family,
/// for `edit_described.rs`'s `TITLE_FONT` reason: the renderer asks for exactly
/// this name. IBM Plex Mono is the app's own face for machine-produced
/// numbers (`Theme.mono`), and monospacing is not decoration here — a
/// proportional timecode's digits change width as they count, so the field
/// twitches thirty times a second in the corner of a frame somebody is
/// trying to watch.
pub(crate) const BURN_IN_FONT: &str = "IBMPlexMono-Regular";

/// The burn-in's type size as a fraction of the canvas HEIGHT, so a 4K
/// review copy and a 1080p one read the same at the same zoom. Smaller than
/// the Caption preset's 0.035 (`CaptionLayout.captionPreset`), because a
/// burn-in is a reference reading a reviewer glances at when they want to
/// name a moment, not the thing being read.
const BURN_IN_SIZE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.03;

---
title: Text clips
description: Add a title to the timeline, type its words, and see what else a text clip can do.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A text clip puts words on the canvas: a title, a name strap, a line of explanation. It sits on a track like any other clip, and it has no source file behind it.

<AtAGlance
  keys="T"
  where={['The Add Text button in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Content']}
  tools={['add_text_clip', 'set_text']}
/>

<Shot
  name="06-clip-text.window"
  alt="A title reading Frame Job selected in the preview, with an orange frame and handles around it. Its clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector's Clip tab is open on the Text sub-tab."
/>

## Add a text clip

Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.

The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds.

It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.

The clip comes in selected, so the inspector opens on its **Text** sub-tab and the canvas shows its handles.

## Change the length

Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.

## Write the words

There are two places to type:

- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Fold it and its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".

In the **Content** box:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text and gives the keys back to the editor |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |

A click anywhere else applies the text too. An unchanged text makes no undo step, and a changed one makes one, **Edit Text**.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.

## Style the clip

The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:

| Section | Page |
| --- | --- |
| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |

The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.

## Place it and add effects

A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:

- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)

Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.

## With an agent

`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time, and it can set the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.

`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

- A caption is a text clip too. If the text is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and the page loses its timing and draws static, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).

## Related

- [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
EOF
cat > text-style.mdx <<'EOF'
---
title: Font and text style
description: Choose a text clip's font and size, then set its colour, alignment, capitals, line spacing and letter spacing.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start folded. Folded, **Font** shows the size and **Style** shows the alignment.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Choose a font

**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.

**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.

When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name, and otherwise uses Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.

See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.

## Set the size

**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.

The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size that suits the canvas, try a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/). They work it out for you.

## Set the colour

**Color** is white by default. Its opacity is set in the colour panel, along with the colour.

## Align the text

| Control | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |

Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.

With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.

## Show the text in capitals

Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.

The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.

## Adjust the spacing

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |

## Reset the style

**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:

- **Color** to white
- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
- **UPPERCASE** off
- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px

It shows while something in the section differs from those values. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Change the style during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.

## With an agent

An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. It isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

- A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The Text tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.

## Related

- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
EOF
cat > edit-text-on-canvas.mdx <<'EOF'
---
title: Edit text on the canvas
description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Type on the canvas

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.

2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.

3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.

</Steps>

The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own text colour on a dark or light panel, not in the clip's colour, so you can always read what you're typing.

**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.

Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Opening the text editor leaves crop mode.

## Apply the text

Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:

- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
- A click anywhere else

Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.

## Start a new line

<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.

## Leave with Esc

Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.

Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?":

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |

## Use an input method

While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.

## Good to know

- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
EOF
cat > text-presets.mdx <<'EOF'
---
title: Text presets
description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look that's sized to your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its face, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
/>

## Apply a preset

<Steps>

1. Select one or more text clips.

2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.

3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.

</Steps>

It's one undo step, named after the preset.

## The four presets

| Preset | Face | Size | Size at 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18, radius 6 |
| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12, radius 8 |

The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.

**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same face at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.

On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, to stay clear of a phone's on-screen controls.

[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.

## How a preset fits the canvas

Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one.

The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.

## What a preset changes

As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.

It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.

## With an agent

There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/)
EOF
cat > text-outline-and-backdrop.mdx <<'EOF'
---
title: Text outline and backdrop
description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Add an outline

Select a text clip, open the **Outline** section of the **Text** sub-tab, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |

Both are greyed while the outline is off. Folded, the section shows the width, or "off".

The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.

## Add a backdrop

Open the **Backdrop** section and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |

All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. Folded, the section shows the padding, or "off".

A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.

## Change them during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.

## Good to know

- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.

The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size that suits the canvas, try a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/). They work it out for you.

## Set the colour

**Color** is white by default. Its opacity is set in the colour panel, along with the colour.

## Align the text

| Control | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |

Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.

With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.

## Show the text in capitals

Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.

The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.

## Adjust the spacing

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |

## Reset the style

**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:

- **Color** to white
- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
- **UPPERCASE** off
- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px

It shows while something in the section differs from those values. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Change the style during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.

## With an agent

An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. It isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

- A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The Text tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.

## Related

- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)

---
title: Edit text on the canvas
description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Type on the canvas

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.

2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.

3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.

</Steps>

The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own text colour on a dark or light panel, not in the clip's colour, so you can always read what you're typing.

**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.

Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Opening the text editor leaves crop mode.

## Apply the text

Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:

- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
- A click anywhere else

Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.

## Start a new line

<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.

## Leave with Esc

Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.

Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?":

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |

## Use an input method

While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.

## Good to know

- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

---
title: Text presets
description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look that's sized to your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its face, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
/>

## Apply a preset

<Steps>

1. Select one or more text clips.

2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.

3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.

</Steps>

It's one undo step, named after the preset.

## The four presets

| Preset | Face | Size | Size at 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18, radius 6 |
| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12, radius 8 |

The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.

**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same face at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.

On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, to stay clear of a phone's on-screen controls.

[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.

## How a preset fits the canvas

Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one.

The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.

## What a preset changes

As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.

It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.

## With an agent

There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/)

---
title: Text outline and backdrop
description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Add an outline

Select a text clip, open the **Outline** section of the **Text** sub-tab, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |

Both are greyed while the outline is off. Folded, the section shows the width, or "off".

The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.

## Add a backdrop

Open the **Backdrop** section and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |

All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. Folded, the section shows the padding, or "off".

A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.

## Change them during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.

## Good to know

- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

---
title: Text clips
description: Add a title to the timeline, type its words, and see what else a text clip can do.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A text clip puts words on the canvas: a title, a name strap, a line of explanation. It sits on a track like any other clip, and it has no source file behind it.

<AtAGlance
  keys="T"
  where={['The Add Text button in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Content']}
  tools={['add_text_clip', 'set_text']}
/>

<Shot
  name="06-clip-text.window"
  alt="A title reading Frame Job selected in the preview, with an orange frame and handles around it. Its clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector's Clip tab is open on the Text sub-tab."
/>

## Add a text clip

Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.

The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds.

It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.

The clip comes in selected, so the inspector opens on its **Text** sub-tab and the canvas shows its handles.

## Change the length

Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.

## Write the words

There are two places to type:

- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Fold it and its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".

In the **Content** box:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text and gives the keys back to the editor |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |

A click anywhere else applies the text too. An unchanged text makes no undo step, and a changed one makes one, **Edit Text**.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.

## Style the clip

The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:

| Section | Page |
| --- | --- |
| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |

The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.

## Place it and add effects

A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:

- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)

Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.

## With an agent

`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time, and it can set the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.

`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

A caption is a text clip too. If the text is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and the page loses its timing and draws static, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).

## Related

- [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)

The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start folded. Folded, **Font** shows the size and **Style** shows the alignment.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Choose a font

**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.

**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.

When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name, and otherwise uses Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.

See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.

## Set the size

**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.

The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size worked out from the canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).

## Set the colour

**Color** is white by default. Set its opacity in the colour panel, along with the colour.

## Align the text

| Control | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |

Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.

With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.

## Show the text in capitals

Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.

The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.

## Adjust the spacing

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |

## Reset the style

**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:

- **Color** to white
- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
- **UPPERCASE** off
- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px

It shows while something in the section differs from those values. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Change the style during a clip

## With an agent

An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. It isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
