---
title: Edit text on the canvas
description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Type on the canvas

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.

2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.

3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.

</Steps>

The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own colours, not the clip's, so you can always read what you're typing.

**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.

Opening the editor leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters it.

## Apply the text

Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:

- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
- A click anywhere else

Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.

## Start a new line

<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.

## Leave with Esc

Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.

Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?":

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |

While the sheet is up, clicking away doesn't apply the text behind your back.

## Use an input method

While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.

## Good to know

- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

---
title: Text presets
description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look, sized to your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its face, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
/>

## Apply a preset

<Steps>

1. Select one or more text clips.

2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.

3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.

</Steps>

It's one undo step, named after the preset.

## The four presets

| Preset | Face | Size | At 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18, radius 6 |
| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12, radius 8 |

The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.

**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same face at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.

On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, to stay clear of a phone's on-screen controls.

[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.

## How a preset fits the canvas

Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one.

The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.

## What a preset changes

As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.

It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.

## With an agent

There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/)

---
title: Text outline and backdrop
description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Add an outline

Select a text clip, open the **Outline** section of the **Text** sub-tab, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |

Both are greyed while the outline is off. Folded, the section shows the width, or "off".

The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.

## Add a backdrop

Open the **Backdrop** section and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |

All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. Folded, the section shows the padding, or "off".

A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.

## Change them during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.

## Good to know

- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.

## With an agent

`set_text` turns either one off by sending an empty value, and sets all of an outline's or a backdrop's settings at once. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. Folded, the section shows the padding, or "off".

A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.

## Change them during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.

## Good to know

- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.

## With an agent

`set_text` turns either one off by sending an empty value, and sets all of an outline's or a backdrop's settings at once. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

---
title: Text clips
description: Add a title to the timeline, type its words, and see what else a text clip can do.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A text clip puts words on the canvas: a title, a name strap, a line of explanation. It sits on a track like any other clip, and it has no source file behind it.

<AtAGlance
  keys="T"
  where={['The Add Text button in the timeline bar', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Content']}
  tools={['add_text_clip', 'set_text']}
/>

<Shot
  name="06-clip-text.window"
  alt="A title reading Frame Job selected in the preview, with an orange frame and handles around it. Its clip is outlined in the timeline, and the inspector's Clip tab is open on the Text sub-tab."
/>

## Add a text clip

Press <kbd>T</kbd>, or click **Add Text** in the timeline bar, the **Aa** button. There's no menu item for it.

The new clip reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, in white, centred on the canvas, and it lasts 5 seconds.

It lands at the playhead on the front-most track if it fits there, and on a new track in front of everything if it doesn't. Either way it's one undo step, **Add Text**. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the front-most track is the nest's own.

The clip comes in selected, so the inspector opens on its **Text** sub-tab and the canvas shows its handles.

## Change the length

Five seconds is only where a text clip starts. With no source file to run out of, you can [trim](/editing/trimming/) it to any length.

## Write the words

There are two places to type:

- **On the canvas.** Double-click the clip in the preview. See [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
- **In the inspector.** Select the clip and use the **Content** section at the top of the **Text** sub-tab. It's the one Text section that starts open. Fold it and its header shows the first line of the text, or "empty".

In the **Content** box:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Return</kbd> | Applies the text and gives the keys back to the editor |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Applies the text the same way, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings |
| <kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd> or <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> | Starts a new line |

A click anywhere else applies the text too. An unchanged text makes no undo step, and a changed one makes one, **Edit Text**.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Content** sets the words at that action's end. Words don't ease from one to another, so the text switches when the action ends.

## Style the clip

The **Text** sub-tab has the rest of a clip's look, and each section has its own page:

| Section | Page |
| --- | --- |
| **Font** and **Style** | [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/) |
| **Outline** and **Backdrop** | [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) |
| **Box** | [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) |
| **Reveal** | [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) |
| **Presets** | [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/) |

The sub-tab shows only when every selected clip is a text clip. With several selected, a change goes to all of them.

## Place it and add effects

A text clip also has a **Picture** sub-tab, with these sections in this order:

- [Transform](/canvas/transform/), for position, scale, rotation and opacity
- [Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/), which isn't shown while a nest is open
- [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/)
- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
- [Reflection](/effects/reflection/)
- [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/)
- [Obscure](/effects/obscure/)

Crop, Corner Radius, Chroma Key and Background aren't offered, because they work on a clip's source pixels. A text clip has no **Color** or **Sound** sub-tab.

## With an agent

`add_text_clip` needs a track and a time, and it can set the words and the whole look in the same call. Unlike <kbd>T</kbd>, it doesn't fall back to a new track: if the clip would overlap another, Frame Job won't add it.

`set_text` changes any mix of a clip's words and typography in one undo step. An agent isn't held to the ranges of the inspector's fields, so a size above 800 px is fine, for example. Position and scale go through `set_video`. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

A caption is a text clip too. If the text is timed word by word, editing it keeps the timings while the number of words stays the same. Change the number of words and the page loses its timing and draws static, and **Content** notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).

## Related

- [Edit text on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)

---
title: Font and text style
description: Choose a text clip's font and size, then set its colour, alignment, capitals, line spacing and letter spacing.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Font** and **Style** sections of the **Text** sub-tab set how a text clip's words look. Select a text clip to reach them. Both start folded. Folded, **Font** shows the size and **Style** shows the alignment.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Font', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Style']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Choose a font

**Family** lists every font family installed on your Mac, plus the ones Frame Job ships with: Source Sans 3, Source Serif 4, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque and IBM Plex Mono.

**Style** lists the faces of that family, such as Regular or SemiBold.

When you change **Family**, Frame Job keeps the current style if the new family has one of that name, and otherwise uses Regular. Both controls make an undo step called **Font**.

See [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) for more on the faces.

## Set the size

**Size** runs from 6 to 800 px, and a new clip starts at 72 px. Type a value or use the quick picks: 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144.

The size is in canvas pixels, so the same number looks smaller on a larger canvas. For a size worked out from the canvas, use a [preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/).

## Set the colour

**Color** is white by default. Set its opacity in the colour panel, along with the colour.

## Align the text

| Control | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Align** | **L**, **C** or **R** | Centre |
| **Vertical** | Top, middle or bottom of the box | Middle |

Both make an undo step called **Alignment**.

With the box on **Auto-size**, the box is as wide as the longest line, so **Align** lines up the shorter lines and a single line doesn't move. In a [fixed-width box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/), it places every line in the box. To move the text itself, drag it on the canvas or use [Transform](/canvas/transform/).

A text box is always as tall as its words, so **Vertical** moves the text by a pixel or two at most.

## Show the text in capitals

Tick **UPPERCASE** to draw the text in capitals. What you typed is kept as you typed it, so unticking the box brings it back. It never changes the number of words, so it's safe on captions timed word by word.

The [canvas text editor](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) shows the text as you typed it, not in capitals.

## Adjust the spacing

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Line spacing** | The space between lines, as a multiple of the font's line height | 1× | 0.5 to 4× |
| **Tracking** | Extra space between letters. Below 0 pulls them together. | 0 px | −20 to 100 px |

## Reset the style

**Reset** in the **Style** section's header puts everything in that section back, in one undo step called **Text Style**:

- **Color** to white
- **Align** to centre and **Vertical** to middle
- **UPPERCASE** off
- **Line spacing** to 1× and **Tracking** to 0 px

It shows while something in the section differs from those values. It doesn't touch the font or the size, and the **Font** section has no **Reset** of its own. To put **Size** back to 72 px, right-click its row and choose **Reset to default**.

## Change the style during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Size**, **Color**, **Line spacing** and **Tracking** ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. **Family**, **Style**, **Align**, **Vertical** and **UPPERCASE** switch when the action ends.

## With an agent

An agent names a font by its one PostScript name, such as `SourceSans3-Bold`, rather than by family and style. It isn't held to the ranges above: a size or line spacing only has to be above 0. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Good to know

A project can name a font this Mac doesn't have. The **Text** sub-tab still opens, showing the first family in the list, and the text draws in a substitute until you install the font or choose another.

## Related

- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)

---
title: Edit text on the canvas
description: Double-click a text clip in the preview to type into it, then apply, add new lines or back out.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

You can type straight into a text clip in the preview, and see the words wrap where they'll sit in the picture.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Return', '⇧Return', 'Esc']}
  where="Double-click a text clip in the preview"
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Type on the canvas

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead so the clip is on the canvas.

2. Double-click the clip. The editor opens over it with all the text selected.

3. Type. The editor grows and wraps as you go, the way the text will once applied.

4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> to apply.

</Steps>

The editor uses the clip's own font, tracking and line spacing at the canvas's zoom, so the lines break where they will in the picture. It draws in the interface's own colours, not the clip's, so you can always read what you're typing.

**UPPERCASE** text shows as you typed it. A rotated clip's editor stays upright, and the text you apply is the same either way.

Opening the editor leaves [crop mode](/canvas/crop/). Double-clicking any other kind of clip enters it.

## Apply the text

Any of these applies the text and closes the editor:

- <kbd>Return</kbd> or keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd>
- <kbd>Tab</kbd>, unless Full Keyboard Access is on in System Settings
- A click anywhere else

Applying is one undo step, **Edit Text**. If the words haven't changed, there's no undo step. After <kbd>Return</kbd> the keys go back to the canvas, so its single-letter keys work again.

## Start a new line

<kbd>⇧Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌥Return</kbd>, <kbd>⌘Return</kbd> and <kbd>⌃Return</kbd> all start a new line. Caps Lock and <kbd>fn</kbd> don't count, so <kbd>Return</kbd> with either of those still applies.

## Leave with Esc

Over unchanged text, <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the editor at once.

Over changed text, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?":

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** | Keeps your text and closes the editor. It's the default, on <kbd>Return</kbd>. |
| **Revert** | Closes the editor and drops your changes. |
| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing. <kbd>Esc</kbd> in the sheet does the same. |

While the sheet is up, clicking away doesn't apply the text behind your back.

## Use an input method

While an input method is composing, <kbd>Return</kbd>, keypad <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Esc</kbd> go to the input method, not the editor. They do their usual jobs again once the composition ends.

## Good to know

- You can only double-click what's on the canvas, and a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) can't be picked there. To change those words, use **Content** in the [Text sub-tab](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#write-the-words).
- The editor always changes the clip's own words, even with an [action](/motion/actions/) selected. To change the words at an action's end, use **Content**.
- On a caption timed word by word, changing the number of words drops the page's timing. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#good-to-know).

## Related

- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

---
title: Text presets
description: Give a text clip a ready-made Title, Subtitle, Lower Third or Caption look, sized to your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A preset gives a text clip a finished look with one click: its face, size, alignment, backdrop and position, sized to fit your canvas.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Presets"
  tools={['set_text', 'set_video']}
/>

## Apply a preset

<Steps>

1. Select one or more text clips.

2. Open the **Presets** section at the bottom of the **Text** sub-tab. It starts folded.

3. Click **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Lower Third** or **Caption**.

</Steps>

It's one undo step, named after the preset.

## The four presets

| Preset | Face | Size | At 1920 × 1080 | Align | Position | Backdrop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Title** | Source Sans 3 Bold | 9 % | 97 px | Centre | Centre of the canvas | None |
| **Subtitle** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 5 % | 54 px | Centre | 18 % of the height below centre | None |
| **Lower Third** | Source Sans 3 SemiBold | 4.5 % | 49 px | Left | 20 % of the width left of centre, 28 % of the height below it | Black at 55 %, padding 18, radius 6 |
| **Caption** | Source Sans 3 Regular | 3.5 % | 38 px | Centre | 38 % of the height below centre | Black at 60 %, padding 12, radius 8 |

The position is where the centre of the text's box sits, so a longer name on a **Lower Third** grows both ways from that point.

**Title** isn't the look a new text clip starts with. That has the same face at a fixed 72 px, where **Title** works its size out from the canvas.

On a canvas taller than wide, **Caption** sits higher, a quarter of the height below centre, to stay clear of a phone's on-screen controls.

[Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) from **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and **File ▸ Import Captions…** use the **Caption** look, and they also wrap at 80 % of the canvas width. The **Caption** button itself leaves the [box](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) as it is.

## How a preset fits the canvas

Sizes are a share of the canvas's shorter side, and positions a share of its width and height. So a preset fits any canvas, and a vertical 1080 × 1920 canvas gets the same text height as a 1920 × 1080 one.

The size is worked out once, from the canvas at the moment you click. Changing the canvas afterwards doesn't apply the preset again.

## What a preset changes

As well as the settings in the table, a preset sets **Vertical** to middle and **Opacity** back to 100 %. **Title** and **Subtitle** take away any backdrop.

It leaves everything else alone, including the words, the colour, the outline, tracking, line spacing, **UPPERCASE**, the box, the reveal, scale and rotation.

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a preset sets that action's end, like any other field.

## With an agent

There's no preset tool. An agent sends the same values through `set_text` and `set_video`. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/)
- [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/)

---
title: Text outline and backdrop
description: Draw a stroke around a text clip's letters, or put a rounded plate behind them, so the words stay readable over any picture.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

White words get lost over a bright shot. An outline draws a stroke around each letter, and a backdrop puts a rounded plate behind the whole text. You can use either or both.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Outline', 'Clip tab ▸ Text ▸ Backdrop']}
  tools="set_text"
/>

## Add an outline

Select a text clip, open the **Outline** section of the **Text** sub-tab, and tick **Outline**. You get a 2 px black stroke.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Width** | The stroke's thickness. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 2 px | 0 to 40 px |
| **Color** | The stroke's colour | Black | |

Both are greyed while the outline is off. Folded, the section shows the width, or "off".

The stroke sits on the edge of each letter, half inside and half outside, so a wide outline thins the letters.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the outline off.

## Add a backdrop

Open the **Backdrop** section and tick **Backdrop**. You get a black plate at 60 % opacity.

| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fill** | The plate's colour and opacity | Black at 60 % | |
| **Padding** | The space between the text and the plate's edge. Quick picks: 0, 8, 12, 24 and 48. | 12 px | 0 to 200 px |
| **Radius** | How round the corners are. Quick picks: 0, 4, 8, 16 and 32. | 8 px | 0 to 200 px |

All three are greyed while the backdrop is off. Folded, the section shows the padding, or "off".

A radius can't go past half the plate's shorter side, so a large radius makes a pill shape and goes no further.

**Reset** in the section's header turns the backdrop off.

## Change them during a clip

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, these controls set the look at that action's end. **Width**, **Padding**, **Radius** and the colours ease towards the new value, and colours blend in OKLab. Turning an outline or a backdrop on or off switches when the action ends.

## Good to know

- Turning an outline or a backdrop off forgets its settings. Turn it on again and it's back to the defaults.
- Both make the clip's box bigger. The margin around the words is whichever is larger, the outline's width or the backdrop's padding, not the two added together. The plate fills that whole box.
- During a [reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/), the backdrop is there at full strength from the first frame, and the words arrive on it. An outline comes and goes with its letters.

## With an agent

`set_text` turns either one off by sending an empty value, and sets all of an outline's or a backdrop's settings at once. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

## Related

- [Font and text style](/text-and-shapes/text-style/)
- [Text presets](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/)
- [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/)

That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers):
15	/>
16	
17	## Add a marker
18	
19	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same.
20	
21	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Two markers can't share a frame, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one beeps and adds nothing.
22	
23	A marker draws on the ruler as a small flag with a thin line down the ruler, in its colour. An ordinary marker's flag is an outline, and a [chapter](#make-a-chapter) marker's is filled. A project can hold up to 1,024 markers.
24	
25	## Move, rename and remove a marker
26	
27	| To | Do this |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. It snaps, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |
30	| Rename a marker | Double-click its flag, or type in its row in the Document tab. |
31	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
32	
33	Each of these is one undo step.
34	
35	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.
36	
37	## Jump between markers
38	
39	**Mark ▸ Next Marker** and **Mark ▸ Previous Marker** pause playback and move the playhead to the marker. Neither has a keyboard shortcut. They beep when there's no marker further in that direction, and they're dimmed when the project has no markers.
40	
41	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
42	
43	## The Markers list
44	
45	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
46	
47	## Make a chapter
...
49	A marker's colour can only be set by an agent, with `add_marker` or `set_marker`. The colour names are the six [clip label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) colours, and any other name draws the marker in the neutral text colour.
50	
51	## Good to know
52	
53	Markers belong to the whole timeline, not to a nest. While a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open:
54	
55	- The ruler shows no markers, and drags don't snap to them.
56	- The three marker commands in the **Mark** menu are off, and pressing <kbd>M</kbd> beeps.
57	- **Go** is disabled, because the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's own start. Its tooltip says to leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>.
58	- The Document tab's list still shows every marker, and its name field, **Chapter** and **Delete** still work.
59	
60	An agent works to the same rule. With a nest open it can't add a marker or move one, but it can rename one, change its colour or chapter setting, or remove it. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
61	
62	## Related
63	
64	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
65	- [The in and out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
66	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/)
